title: Finite-projective Hom is tensor with the explicit dual
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, with module sheaves on the bottom-topology one-object ringed site [def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map]. Let P,Q be cochain complexes. Assume there are integers a,b such that P^n vanishes whenever n<a or b<n, and every evaluated term P^n is finite projective. Put D=Hom_A^\bullet(P,A[0]), the explicit dual construction of [lem-pc-perfect-ring-dual-term-flat]. Then there exists a chain isomorphism Tot(D\otimes_A Q)\cong Hom_A^\bullet(P,Q), for the shared total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and Hom [def-pur-hom-complex]. No boundedness or K-flatness of Q is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0A6A, lemma-base-change-RHom, clause (1), expanded chain-level evaluation; Tag 0ATK, lemma-base-change-evaluation-map, clause (1)

proof.text: Evaluate on the one-object bottom-topology site to identify internal Hom and tensor with linear Hom and module tensor. For a finite free M the evaluation map Hom(M,A) tensor N -> Hom(M,N), lambda tensor y |-> (x |-> lambda(x)y), has inverse f |-> sum_i e_i^* tensor f(e_i). The basis identities prove both composites are identities. If M is finite projective, choose maps i:M -> A^r and p:A^r -> M with pi=id. Naturality under precomposition restricts the free evaluation isomorphism to the images of the splitting idempotents and supplies inverse maps for M. Apply this to M=P^(-r) and N=Q^s. Projection identifies the r-th dual term with Hom(P^(-r),A).

For each n, reindex r+s=n by p=-r. Bounds on P mean only a<=p<=b can contribute. All remaining terms vanish, so the coproduct over r+s=n and the product over p become the same finite biproduct. Take the direct sum of the evaluation isomorphisms with coefficient (-1)^(rs). This yields degreewise mutually inverse maps Tot(D tensor Q)^n <-> Hom(P,Q)^n. The tensor differential has terms d_D lambda tensor y and (-1)^r lambda tensor d_Q y. Since d_D lambda=-(-1)^r lambda d_P, the first term after evaluation has sign (-1)^(rs+r+s+1) and the second has sign (-1)^(rs). These are the precomposition and postcomposition signs of d_Q f - (-1)^(r+s) f d_P. Thus the forward maps commute with differentials; their inverses do also, by cancellation. They form the asserted chain isomorphism and can be transported back to sheaves. Q may be unbounded, and a>b simply makes all terms zero.
